catalogue_requests.reason: cap.motion.home.v1 publishes optional axes and speed_scale inputs, but the upstream Gantry.home has no axis selection and no speed argument: it sends GRBL's standard all-axis homing command. The package uses an extension with an empty input rather than accept fields the native call cannot honor.

cap.motion.stop.v1 publishes an optional deceleration input, but the upstream stop is a GRBL real-time feed hold with no deceleration argument (it verifies Hold afterwards). The package uses an extension with an empty input as its safe-state action.

The catalogue has no class for releasing a feed hold. Gantry.resume writes the GRBL real-time cycle-start character and is the device's declared recovery after an operator reset (reenable=True); the package declares it as an empty-input extension so the recovery contract is explicit and CORE-086 can refuse it while latched.

notes:
Passed on the fake backend with python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/labs/ursa-laboratories__cubos --backend fake (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). The check-report has no findings in G1-G9 (no warnings). Model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null, so the loader refuses the R2 hardware backend until a human signs it; the hardware factory and the cubos package were never imported or run, and no hardware test was performed. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card names PythonObjectDriver, but the package is a direct decorated Driver over the card entry symbol cubos.gantry.gantry:Gantry. The motion actions combine native blocking calls with a position read-back and a cap.motion.cartesian_pose.v1 output schema, which the family's static result map cannot express. All five card entry symbols were confirmed in the clone (Gantry, SartoriusPicus2Pipette, ExcelitasUVCuring, ThorlabsUVVisCCS, OpentronsPipette); only Gantry is integrated, because one package serves one device. device_kind is robot.arm because cap.motion.cartesian_pose.v1 binds only robot.arm (catalog show); the machine is a three-axis Cartesian gantry, not an articulated arm. COVERAGE: reads position (Gantry.get_coordinates x/y/z in mm), status (Gantry.get_status) and healthy (Gantry.is_healthy); actions x-cap.ursa-laboratories.home_axes.v1 (Gantry.home -> GRBL $H), cap.motion.cartesian_pose.v1 (Gantry.move_to x/y/z), x-cap.ursa-laboratories.stop_motion.v1 (Gantry.stop, safe_state=True) and x-cap.ursa-laboratories.resume_motion.v1 (Gantry.resume, reenable=True); @estop calls the same native stop; teardown closes the controller. There is no write: feed rates, travel and GRBL settings live in the machine configuration and no text states a machine-independent bound. The X/Y/Z targets are Limit.operator_required because the clone stores the travel envelope in each machine's calibrated working_volume (docs/gantry.md:155-169) and the upstream Gantry only validates that coordinates are finite; site-limits.example.json is an operator example and fills the envelope for G8, and until a site overlay exists every move is refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET. SAFETY: risk R2 from real mechanical motion; estop_physical_ref cites the machine E-stop kept within reach (docs/operator-ui/gantry.md:32); the safe-state action and @estop use Gantry.stop -> Mill.stop, a GRBL real-time feed hold sent outside the command/response cycle and verified by a Hold status query. This is a pause, not a power removal: the documented Resume can continue held motion, so a reset only releases the latch and the explicit reenable action is required; there is no @reset hook. A feed hold does not cancel a queued multi-axis move: the pending execute_command stays in its wait loop and the held path remains until the operator checks it and resumes. NOT COVERED: GRBL soft limits, alarms, end stops, homing timeout behaviour, serial transport details, jog, soft reset/unlock, prepare_for_protocol_run, the optional travel_z argument, and all other CubOS instruments and host applications. The hardware native factory (.native:connect) imports cubos.gantry.gantry:Gantry, constructs Gantry with the site's machine config mapping, calls connect(port), and sends no motion; it requires the upstream package installed from packages/core of the clone and a calibrated machine config, and cannot be validated without hardware. The fake is an analytic in-memory stand-in, not a recording: starting position, status strings and counters are placeholders and nothing is replayed; it models the Hold state and resume and refuses motion while held, while the real controller queues motion and _wait_until_idle times out, and it models no serial timing, GRBL planner, alarms or end stops. No ROS or other transport is involved, and no hardware run is claimed.

MODEL REVIEW (gpt-6.1-sol, a model and not a human, 2026-11-17; reviewed_by stays null): Model review traced Gantry through Mill and found that motion after latch reset could reach the native queue while Hold was active, a defect hidden by the fake's immediate refusal. driver.py now checks controller state before move/home dispatch, preserves Alarm recovery by homing, narrows overbroad Facts and describes the safe state as Hold acknowledgement with the queued path retained. Updated native.py, test_driver.py and facts.md, regenerated reference.json and REFERENCE.md, and refreshed check-report.json. The new refusal regressions failed before the fix, and the final fake gate, package tests and strict collector pass. For the human reviewer: The feed hold checks one status containing Hold; it does not poll for stationary axes, remove power or cancel the held path. Reset releases the latch only; the separate re-enable can continue previously queued motion and requires inspection of that path. The readiness check cannot exclude an external client changing state after its read. Serial readers share the stream and native calls can exceed the MHS stop budget; unconfirmed stops stay failed and latched. The physical-stop reference is an operator-document instruction, without wiring or measured latency. Connection may probe other ports even when a preferred port is supplied and changes WPos reporting, G90 and feed rate; no G21 command establishes length units in the reviewed gantry code. Other card instruments are not integrated. No upstream import, serial connection or hardware execution occurred in model review.
